pr_title: WebGLRenderer: Fix texture unit allocation of morph textures.
pr_body:
Related issue: Fixed #22619

**Description**

This PR ensures that similar to bone textures, morph textures allocated the same texture unit.
pr_comments: I guess we need `r133.1` with this fix.

issue_context.title: Rendering issues with shadow-casting, morphed meshes.
issue_context.body:
His shadow is working so hard but he just sits [there](https://threejs.org/examples/webgl_animation_multiple.html) motionless:


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/242577/135541123-36ee92d3-a2d6-4c76-a661-dde9438d6b35.mp4
comments:
That is strange. On my Windows machine, the second parrot is completely missing.

I also see the following warning in Chrome:

> [.WebGL-00001F28000A6A00] GL_INVALID_OPERATION: Two textures of different types use the same sampler location.

This issue is related to the new morph target code. And it only appears when using shadows. As a temporary workaround, affected users can fallback to `WebGL1Renderer` or disable shadows if possible. 

It is strange that [webgl_shadowmap](https://threejs.org/examples/webgl_shadowmap) does not show this issue.
The E2E screenshot also shows the wrong result. There should be two parrots visible.

review_comments: I don't think the `!! object.geometry` statements make sense. Render items always have a geometry, no?
Ah wait, we need this for `ImmediateRenderObject`.
I wonder if we could remove `ImmediateRenderObject` 🤔. This would noticeably simplify the renderer. And in that way,`WebGPURenderer` does not have to support `ImmediateRenderObject`.
